blocks.text: Maimuni thus abandoned the Talmudic determination of the colour as "sky-blue" and instead took תכלת to be the brown colour. However, Maimuni's explanation is in itself already incorrect; for of the cuttlefish it is known only that the Romans in the first century used its juice as ink for writing. None of the ancient writers mentions the use of the cuttlefish's juice for dyeing; only conjurers smeared lamp and lights with that juice, whereby those present appeared copper-coloured in the [p. 285] face (Plin. h. n. 32, 10, 52 and on this Harduin).

The cuttlefish is, moreover, so common that in Italy it is frequently caught and eaten by the lowest class of the people, whereas the Talmud describes the חלזון as rare. The statement that it is seen only once in 70 years is a formula of exaggeration by which rarity is figuratively denoted. After all this, Maimuni's interpretation of חלזון may well be dropped.
It may be remarked here in passing that in the Book Jezirah the word חלזון denotes the oyster*) and in the Jerusalem Talmud Sabbat 3b the same word denotes the whirring locust (§. 387).
